title: Object Storage
objectives: Explain Object Storage with measurable requirements and failure modes
Apply Object Storage to a high-traffic India-scale scenario in an interview

cards.title: text
cards.body: Interview lens on Object Storage: open with actors, peak traffic shape, and explicit non-goals so the conversation stays bounded like a production RFC review (topic 61).

cards.title: text
cards.body: Mental model for Object Storage: map each user action to a synchronous vs asynchronous hop, then mark which hops need strong invariants versus where stale reads are tolerable.

cards.title: diagram
cards.body: Walk a hot read path for Object Storage: client → DNS/TLS → edge → service → cache → store. Call out where you would measure p95 and which hop fails first under 10× diurnal peak.

cards.title: text
cards.body: Failure mode in Object Storage: retries without idempotency, cache stampedes, or unbounded fan-out often hurt before raw CPU; name the guardrail you add first for this topic.

cards.title: animation
cards.body: Say aloud for Object Storage: (1) user story in one sentence, (2) two numbers (QPS + data size), (3) one trade-off you will revisit in the deep dive.

questions.prompt: For Object Storage, which first step best reduces ambiguity in a system design interview?

choices.label: List user actions, scale, and latency/durability targets

questions.explanation: Strong interviews anchor on requirements and SLOs before components.

questions.prompt: Where is the first saturation point in a naive single-region Object Storage design under flash traffic?
questions.explanation: Unsharded OLTP primaries usually exhaust connections/IOPS before stateless tiers.

questions.prompt: Order a crisp interview flow when presenting Object Storage.

items.label: Deep dive hot path and failures

questions.explanation: Numbers before boxes keeps trade-offs honest.

questions.prompt: Object Storage: 2.4M read requests/day spread uniformly. Estimate average read QPS (nearest integer).
questions.workedAnswer: 2.4M/day ≈ 27.8 QPS average; plan higher for peak factors.
questions.explanation: Convert daily volume to per-second capacity before sizing caches and DB pools.

questions.prompt: Choose an approach to handle 5× lunch-hour spikes for Object Storage.

rationaleOptions.label: Stateless tiers absorb burst without one machine ceiling
Caching shifts read load off the primary
Vertical scale cannot survive AZ loss by itself

questions.explanation: Horizontal stateless scaling plus caching is the common interview answer for read-heavy bursts.

questions.prompt: Which NON-functional requirement is most central to Object Storage?

choices.label: Correctness under retries and partial failures

questions.explanation: Distributed systems fail partially; interviews probe how you preserve invariants.

flashcards.front: What is the core interview takeaway for Object Storage?
flashcards.back: Connect user journeys to SLOs, then justify components and trade-offs for Object Storage.

flashcards.front: Name one pitfall when discussing Object Storage.
flashcards.back: Skipping scale numbers, ignoring retries/idempotency, or mixing AuthN with AuthZ.

flashcards.front: Which metric would you cite first for Object Storage?
flashcards.back: p95 latency on the hot path plus error rate on writes/reads that affect revenue or safety.
